title: Uniqueness of Explore's APIs
question: Per API in the public Explore catalog: how distinct is its description from its nearest neighbours, how crowded is its field, and are energy and market APIs per-country copies?

issues.text: Uniqueness of the data is measured through the descriptions: a proxy.
issues.fix: Read the nearest neighbours next to every score, and check twins by their sample answers.

issues.text: 'Per-country copy' is not a field of the catalog.
issues.fix: Measure it as place_effect: the change in distinct when place names are kept.

issues.text: The catalog changes: new APIs move every score.
issues.fix: Note the catalog's updated time; rerun the dashboard.

alternatives.question: Do APIs from one provider score lower than independent APIs in the same field?
alternatives.why: Tests vendor families, the strongest near-copies.

alternatives.question: Do the most unique APIs get used in more dashboards?
alternatives.why: Expands to usage; needs the dashboards' API lists.

alternatives.question: Is distinct lower for APIs with short descriptions?

hypotheses.statement: APIs in an energy or markets category have a lower distinct than the rest.
hypotheses.null: Their mean distinct equals the rest's.

hypotheses.statement: For energy and market APIs, removing place names lowers distinct more than for the rest (per-country copies).
hypotheses.null: The mean place_effect is the same in both groups.

concepts.label: API
concepts.description: An Explore catalog item of kind api.

concepts.label: Distinctness
concepts.why: The text half of the score.

strategy.detail: TF-IDF over title, tags, summary, description; cosine; mean of the 5 nearest.
n = other APIs in the least crowded category.
'energy' or 'markets' anywhere in a category path.
Run the similarity twice, with and without the place-name list.

data.request: Each API's example answer (its first example query), to compare what the APIs return rather than how they are described
data.source: the APIs themselves, through Explore's example queries
data.why: Descriptions are a proxy for the data.

method.summary: Mean distinct and mean place_effect in energy & markets against the rest, with Welch's t.

steps.title: TF-IDF and nearest neighbours
steps.detail: JavaScript: vectors, cosine, 10 nearest, places removed and kept.

steps.title: Score v1 and variants
steps.detail: Polars: distinct for k = 3, 5, 10 and places kept; rarity; score; percentile.

steps.title: Energy & markets
steps.detail: Category path contains energy or markets.

steps.title: Welch t and sensitivity
steps.detail: t = −2.0 on distinct, 2.5 on place_effect: weak support for energy; robust ranking (ρ ≥ 0.97).

caveats: Measures descriptions, not the APIs' data.
The catalog changes; categories are the catalog's at fetch time.
Stop words and place names are a fixed English list.
Rarity uses the least crowded category, so adding a category can raise a score.
